content.content: When deccy opens a draft, the deccy CLI shall record in that draft's record a content-identity base of the node's owned set — one entry for every path the set holds, each the identity of that path's content.
content.rationale:
The trigger is the opening and only the opening, because qrqsxyzz fixes both: a draft's record first exists when the opening writes it, the workspace the draft is written in is created then, and a base taken at any later moment would describe content the caller never saw, so the requirement takes the moment that node already names instead of inventing a second one. The actor is the deccy CLI because the opening is a call the CLI makes and the record is the registry-local object the CLI keeps (qrqsxyzz, owyntkvw). The destination is that draft's record because qrqsxyzz puts the base there and nowhere else — one field of the one document the opening writes, with no second file and no marker anywhere — and because owyntkvw has already settled what a record is: a registry-local object keyed by a handle, with its node, edit and workspace as its only references, and everything else it carries a value of the same kind as the state the opening writes. Recording the base in the record therefore fills a carried field owyntkvw describes rather than making a fourth reference, and it moves nothing: the handle stays the key, the three references stay three, and the record is not made a node document.

The object is a content-identity base, and both halves belong to prerequisites rather than to this requirement. That the base is a content identity is qrqsxyzz: it is a value per path determined by that path's content and by nothing else, equal content giving an equal entry and different content a different one, and it is not a change id, an edit, a workspace, a path name or the tree of a change. The requirement therefore asks for the identity of a path's content and fixes no algorithm, length or textual form, which qrqsxyzz leaves open. That it is the node's owned set is xzxtxymq's boundary: a change owns exactly its node document plus the repo-relative paths its content.ref lists when ref is an array, and the node document alone when ref is inline.

The coverage clause is those two settlements read as a requirement, not a third rule. 'One entry for every path the set holds' is the extent qrqsxyzz already gives the base — an entry for every path of the owned set at that moment — with the set itself fixed by xzxtxymq, so it neither widens the base to the working copy's tree, the change's whole tree or paths no ref of the node names, nor narrows it to the paths a call happens to name. 'Each the identity of that path's content' keeps the entry per path rather than one value over the set, which is what qrqsxyzz's value-per-path already means: the identity is that path's, drawn from the content that path holds, so a path the set has gained or lost is a difference in the base by that same rule (qrqsxyzz, xzxtxymq).

Everything else is deliberately unstated. The encoding of a content identity — algorithm, length, textual form and whether the base is one field holding an entry per path or one field per path — is open in qrqsxyzz, so naming it here would close a choice that node leaves open. The comparison against the owned set at landing, the refusal that names the differing paths, and the record's state and lifetime are settlements qrqsxyzz and owyntkvw already hold, and restating them would reopen them rather than license the opening clause. The record's path, its other fields, the handle and the three references are likewise owyntkvw's and qrqsxyzz's; the requirement mentions the record only as the destination qrqsxyzz already gives the base.
